change: Shared direct metric/vector slot substitution replaces tuple pattern families; epsilon cleanup avoids per-node Schoonschip and repeats whole-expression cleanup only after productive epsilon rewrites.
scope: Canonical tagged rank-one vectors, exact representation/dimension/index matching, opaque scalar parameters, and settings-controlled chain/trace bodies. Existing trace-order behavior is the baseline.
timing_method: Five warm samples per method, methods interleaved with rotating order; target 8ms batches, at least one call. Both Idenso runs pinned CPU6 on a shared host, dev-optim opt-level2/debug-info2. Input construction, validation, output snapshots and calibration excluded; output destruction included. Baseline driver links the saved pre-change Idenso library. FORM fresh measurements run on CPU3 and include amortized startup, parsing, trace4, sorting and cleanup.
count_semantics: terms and output_terms count only top-level Add arity; factorized numerators are not expanded. FORM generated_terms counts sorter submissions and sorted_terms counts collected monomials; neither measures peak resident memory.

methods.metric_contractor_only: Private production-source contractor with chain bodies enabled and vector-source contraction disabled; excludes normalization and repeated-index guard.
methods.guarded_metric_contractor: Repeated-index scan followed by that same metric-only contractor when needed.
methods.metric_schoonschip: Public Schoonschip with chain bodies enabled and rank-one source contraction disabled; includes bracket/dot normalization.
methods.full_schoonschip: Public Schoonschip with chain bodies and tagged rank-one contractions enabled.
methods.full_gamma: Public simplify_gamma on each case gamma_input snapshot, not its prepared cleanup input.

source_hash_note: Current final source hashes are captured at aggregation. Epsilon cfg(test) assertions and HEP fixtures were amended after timing; the full source text therefore is not asserted identical to the timed build. Production code is unchanged. The measured executable/library identities and original Cargo artifact record are recorded separately.
reproduction: taskset -c 6 cargo run --offline -p idenso --profile dev-optim --example metric_contraction_benchmark -- /tmp/gamma-cleanup-benchmark 5 8

methodology.wall: One warmup process, then three measured processes. Six batches per process; entire wall time divided by total traces. Includes process startup, parsing/input normalization, trace4, sorting, count printing, drop and shutdown. Polynomial printing and exact checks excluded.
methodology.cpu: FORM internal timer covers trace4 plus .sort after input preparation; median last five of six batches, divided by traces per batch; median across three measured processes. Millisecond timer resolution applies per batch.
methodology.counts: Generated terms count StoreTerm submissions to sorter; sorted terms count final monomials after trace4+.sort. Neither is peak resident terms. Separate untimed run writes normalized input and complete polynomial. This artifact reuses that earlier untimed run; fresh timing processes also check the expected sorted-term count in every batch.
methodology.scope: Independent p_i vectors and explicit4D Lorentz indices a,b,c,d,mu_i. No numeric/on-shell specialization. FORM fully normalizes external metrics before trace4. Idenso input construction is excluded from its timer; amortized FORM wall includes parsing/input preparation.
methodology.host: Shared host; CPU3 affinity inherited by child processes. Results are measurements, not a claim of equivalence based on term counts.

from pathlib import Path
import hashlib,json,re,statistics,subprocess,time
ROOT=Path(__file__).parent
INPUTS=json.load(open(ROOT/'inputs.json'))
FORM=INPUTS['form_executable']
REPETITIONS={'order_sensitive_12':600,'external_metrics_12':600,'ordinary_odd_8':3000,'ordinary_even2_8':5000,'ordinary_even4_10':400,'ordinary_cyclic_12':150,'axial_odd_8':3000,'axial_even4_10':1000,'axial_crossing_12':1500,'free_8':600,'free_12':40,'axial_12':150}
records=[]
for case in INPUTS['cases']:
    n=REPETITIONS[case['case']]
    program='Off Statistics;\n'+INPUTS['header']+f"""#do batch=1,6
#do j=1,{n}
Local F`j'={case['expression']};
#enddo
.sort
#reset timer
trace4,1;
.sort
#write "BATCH_CPU_MS=`timer_'"
#$n=termsin_(F1);
#write "TERMS=%$",$n
Drop;
.sort
#enddo
.end
"""
    path=ROOT/f"{case['case']}-timing.frm";path.write_text(program)
    wall=[];cpu=[];raw_cpu=[];raw_logs=[]
    for sample in range(4):
        started=time.perf_counter_ns()
        p=subprocess.run([FORM,'-q',str(path)],cwd=ROOT,capture_output=True,text=True,check=True)
        elapsed=(time.perf_counter_ns()-started)/(n*6)
        path.with_suffix(f'.{sample}.log').write_text(p.stdout)
        raw_logs.append(p.stdout)
        times=list(map(int,re.findall(r'BATCH_CPU_MS=(\d+)',p.stdout)))
        counts=list(map(int,re.findall(r'TERMS=(\d+)',p.stdout)))
        assert len(times)==6 and counts==[case['sorted_terms']]*6,(times,counts)
        if sample:
            wall.append(elapsed);cpu.append(statistics.median(times[1:])*1e6/n);raw_cpu.append(times)

    return {'path': str(path), 'sha256': sha(path), 'bytes': path.stat().st_size}

    assert samples and all(math.isfinite(value) and value > 0 for value in samples)
    assert math.isclose(statistics.median(samples), median, rel_tol=1e-12)

# Residual gamma cleanup phase timings

This standalone driver reads saved, already evaluated axial traces of lengths 6, 8, 10, and 12. Every measured rewrite leaves each expression exactly unchanged. Parsing, fixture initialization, correctness checks, and JSON output are excluded from timings. Outputs are destroyed inside the timed loop. Cases and methods rotate across five process-local rounds on CPU6; batch sizes target 10ms after warm-up. `raw.jsonl` contains all 380 samples; `summary.json` records medians and ranges.

`bracket.rs`, `dots.rs`, and `epsilon.rs` are copied from current production with unit tests removed. Epsilon adds thin wrappers exposing the existing presence check and exact candidate visitor. Dots adds wrappers containing each existing normalization stage. No production files were modified for profiling. `production-sources.json` records original hashes; `prepare.py` reproduces source extraction.

Measured methods:

- `ContainsEpsilon`: existing recursive epsilon-presence predicate (short-circuits after finding one).
- `RepeatedIndices`: production explicit repeated-index scan (false on every case).
- `Brackets`: complete private bracket normalizer, including its bottom-up traversal.
- `Dots` / `CopiedDots`: complete production / copied dot normalization; each contains the five following stages.
- `DotNestedVectors`: eligible rank-one vector-in-vector traversal and replacement.
- `DotRedundantMetrics`: redundant compact metric traversal/fixed point.
- `DotVectorPowers`: vector-power pattern replacement over the expression.
- `DotMetricPowers`: metric-power pattern replacement over the expression.
- `DotMetricTraces`: metric-trace pattern replacement over the expression.
- `EpsilonCandidates`: the exact new Pow/Mul epsilon visitor; no identities fire.
- `EpsilonFull` / `CopiedEpsilonFull`: complete production / copied epsilon simplification.
- `Schoonschip`: complete production Schoonschip fixed point with default settings. On these inputs its slot-contraction branch is skipped after the repeated-index scan.
- `Chainify` / `CollectChains`: public chain phases, separately.
- `CollectGammaChains`: complete public chain collection, including its two bracket passes.
- `GammaTerminal`: complete gamma simplification starting from the terminal output, rather than from an unevaluated trace.

The copied complete dot/epsilon methods and every stage were checked against the linked production result. Independent stage medians are useful attribution estimates; summing them is not an exact decomposition because code placement, caches, and caller boundaries differ.

Reproduce in the repository development environment:

```sh
source /tmp/feynkit-docs-dev-env.sh
python /tmp/gamma-cleanup-improvements/phases/prepare.py
```

Compile using the exact argument array in `build-command.json`, with `CARGO_CRATE_NAME=cleanup_phases`. Then:

```sh
taskset -c 6 /tmp/gamma-cleanup-improvements/phases/driver 5 > /tmp/gamma-cleanup-improvements/phases/raw.jsonl
python /tmp/gamma-cleanup-improvements/phases/summarize.py
```

These measurements do not change simplification algorithms or distribute any factorized expressions.
